about.title: Santa Maria Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Santa Maria's streets carry a lot of everyday traffic, and the public record shows what that adds up to. In 2025, the city logged 412 injury collisions. Those crashes left 562 people hurt and took 7 lives. Broadway, Main Street, Blosser Road and Donovan Road account for the largest share of reported collisions, and Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. are when reports cluster most. If one of those numbers is you or someone in your family, the paperwork that follows can feel heavier than the crash itself. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect people injured in Santa Maria car accidents with an independent personal injury attorney who handles cases on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. California gives you two years to file, though a claim involving a city or county vehicle in Santa Barbara County may need to be started within six months. Before you talk to the other driver's insurer, it helps to have someone in your corner.

whyChoose.title: Why Santa Maria Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Pure comparative fault works in your favor
items.desc: California does not shut you out just because you may share some blame for a crash on Main Street. Your recovery is reduced by your percentage of fault, not erased, and an attorney can push back when an insurer inflates that percentage.

items.title: Deadlines that differ by defendant
items.desc: Most Santa Maria car accident claims must be filed within two years, but a crash involving a government vehicle or agency can require a claim within six months. Knowing which clock applies early prevents a valid case from expiring.

items.title: No cap on pain and suffering, no fee up front
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages in ordinary car accident cases, and network attorneys work on contingency. You pay nothing unless there is a recovery, and LawProactive's connection service is always free.

items.question: The other driver's insurance adjuster wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are not required to give the other driver's insurer a recorded statement, and it is generally wise to decline until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can later be used to minimize what you are owed. Politely tell them you will be in touch through your representative.

items.question: I was hit on Broadway during Friday rush hour and there were several witnesses. What should I do now?
items.answer: Late Friday afternoon is when Santa Maria collision reports peak, so witnesses may be hard to track down if you wait. Write down names and numbers now, photograph the scene and vehicle damage if you have not already, and request the police report from the responding agency. Preserving this evidence early gives an attorney far more to work with.

items.question: What does it cost to use LawProactive and then hire the attorney?
items.answer: LawProactive charges nothing to connect you with an independent attorney. The attorneys in our network handle Santa Maria car accident cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless they recover money for you. Any fee agreement is set out in writing before the attorney begins work, and you decide whether to move forward.
